entries.postTitle: Outgrowing Old Identities

captions.threads:
1/4

nobody warns you that the life you built so carefully can start feeling like someone else's costume. you're wearing it perfectly. the fit was immaculate three years ago. but somewhere between that version of you and now, your shoulders changed shape, your breathing patterns shifted, what used to fit snug now restricts.

2/4

the weird part? everyone sees the costume working. they compliment the tailoring. they want to know how you got the seams so precise. meanwhile you're standing in the mirror wondering if taking it off means disappointing people who believed in the image more than they knew you.

3/4

what i've learned is that outgrowing doesn't mean the old thing was wrong. it means you're not the same person who needed it. that identity served a purpose, built something real, got you somewhere necessary. honoring that while admitting it no longer fits, that's the actual work. not burning bridges to the person you were, just gently setting them down.

4/4

the relief comes when you stop asking permission to change. when you accept that evolution isn't betrayal, it's just what happens when you stop pretending the costume still fits perfectly.

captions.threads:
1/4

nobody warns you that the life you built so carefully can start feeling like someone else's costume. you're wearing it perfectly. the fit was immaculate three years ago. but somewhere between that version of you and now, your shoulders changed shape, your breathing patterns shifted, what used to fit snug now restricts.

2/4

the weird part? everyone sees the costume working. they compliment the tailoring. they want to know how you got the seams so precise. meanwhile you're standing in the mirror wondering if taking it off means disappointing people who believed in the image more than they knew you.

3/4

what i've learned is that outgrowing doesn't mean the old thing was wrong. it means you're not the same person who needed it. that identity served a purpose, built something real, got you somewhere necessary. honoring that while admitting it no longer fits, that's the actual work. not burning bridges to the person you were, just gently setting them down.

4/4

the relief comes when you stop asking permission to change. when you accept that evolution isn't betrayal, it's just what happens when you stop pretending the costume still fits perfectly.
